findings.title: Prior released values disappear from the redactor during cancellation
findings.observation: After one successful secret fill, a later action can fail while stop() has already cleared secretValues, runtime values and authored inputs. Catch builds knownValues from the cleared inventories; pushing only the current resolvedValue protects the current argument but not an earlier released secret. A deferred browser close lets the diagnostics sink remain reachable. The actual production GuidedRuntime then emits the prior synthetic released value unchanged to three sinks.
evidence: Independent prior-secret-cancel probe: all three leak booleans true; controlled browser ports, no real Chromium/Core/PG join.
Existing runner-diagnostic-cancel-red addresses the current-argument lifetime, not this prior-secret interleaving.
findings.proposedExactReversibleRemediation: R: create a dispatch-local bounded redaction snapshot/redactor containing all previously released secret values, runtime values, relevant authored values and the current resolved argument before the first await that can race stop. Capture the non-authoritative diagnostics sink reference if needed for a consumed action. Use that immutable redaction capability for scalar scrubbing through callback/diagnostic/stderr completion; clear local references in dispatch finally. Keep stop synchronous for authority revocation/global inventory erasure and keep browser shutdown unblocked. Do not retain action capability, defer cancellation, add raw channels or persist the snapshot.
findings.requiredVerification: A prior successful released secret followed by a different action plus cancel/expiry/context loss: raw synthetic value observed privately, [REDACTED] and zero literal/encoded hits at all three sinks. Exercise both immediate and delayed close, current and prior values, diagnostics write/callback failure. Then source-bound compiled-child/Core/PG joined all-sink scans.

findings.classification: confirmed classification weakness; actual browser postwrite trigger not reproduced
findings.title: Substring matching promotes generic CDP exceptions to positive no-effect knowledge
findings.observation: Any exception description containing TARGET_CHANGED or an allowed policy token becomes PasswordNoEffect. A controlled CDP-port result with an unrelated TypeError description mentioning TARGET_CHANGED is classified noEffect=true. This does not prove a real Chromium postwrite trigger; it proves the classifier is broader than the private trusted prewrite refusal contract. Generic native exception text is not effect evidence.
findings.proposedExactReversibleRemediation: R: return a closed, internally tagged prewrite-refusal result from the private collector checks, with a bounded code allowlist and exact host validation. Keep host pre-invocation guards typed. Treat all CDP exceptionDetails/transport/native exceptions after invocation as generic TARGET_CHANGED with unknown effect unless that private structural refusal fact is present. Avoid deriving noEffect from message substrings. This is an internal port representation, not new external wire authority/status.
findings.requiredVerification: Successful write followed by arbitrary exception text containing each guard token remains unknown; actual prewrite private refusal remains REFUSED/FAILED as appropriate. Include navigation-after-write and transport-loss cases.

findings.classification: design completeness question; conservative backend behavior is approved
findings.title: Closed guided outcome cannot transmit every positive secret-use fact
findings.observation: The current ledger carries no per-secret usage/no-effect fact. Generic failures are labeled ACK_LOST even when actual acknowledgement loss is not known. Approved backend OK→USED and all non-success→UNKNOWN_OUTCOME is truthful and must remain conservative. It cannot distinguish a trusted prewrite refusal from generic native uncertainty, or a known completed fill whose later liveness/callback path failed. Prior committed positive facts must remain immutable. This is a completeness gap, not permission to infer REFUSED or audit ACK_LOST from a label.
findings.proposedExactReversibleRemediation: Retain approved conservative projection immediately. Apply guided ruling below only as a proposed future architecture decision, requiring PO acceptance/contract revalidation before any implementation. Generic/partial errors must not introduce new authority.

designRulings.decision: A narrowly explicit C6 oracle correction is necessary for a deterministic positive control on the mandated single isolated collector primitive; no second fill/raw-value production channel.
designRulings.reasoning: All deliberately thrown collector refusal messages are fixed code strings and host normalization removes generic native details. The primitive does not use Playwright.fill actionability polling, so the existing /slow readonly timeout cannot force its native raw exception to contain the released argument. An unforeseen Chromium/CDP exception could contain it; this review makes no universal impossibility claim about every browser error. Forcing a deterministic canary-bearing error by injection is injection, not authentic native causation. Retaining the literal native-positive assertion as satisfied would be false.
designRulings.proposedExactOracleText: C6: Execute an authentic refusal/failure through the sole production isolated-collector/CDP password primitive. Privately observe the raw failure in volatile test memory at the declared boundary; for the current trusted refusal path assert code-only TARGET_CHANGED and no released canary. Preserve the supplementary Playwright.fill native timeout probe with raw-canary-positive, safe-[REDACTED]-positive and post-redaction-no-canary assertions. Execute the injected actual released-value production GuidedRuntime control and require [REDACTED], redaction before interpolation/bounds, unchanged authoritative hash-only journal and all sink bounds. Across the native, injected and supplementary controls and real in-flight timeout/cancel/context-loss cases, require zero literal/encoded released-canary hits in child stdout/stderr, relay output, step failure, manifest, callbacks, diagnostic sidecar, authoritative journal and parent log in actual joined Core/PostgreSQL/compiled-child runs. Parent DEBUG=pw:* must be absent from the child environment while the run proceeds. Native prewrite refusals and generic post-invocation uncertainty must retain truthful effect classification.

designRulings.currentDecision: Preserve approved backend conservative OK→USED and non-success→UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; immutable prior committed positives. ACK_LOST text alone never proves actual acknowledgement loss.
knowledgeRules: USED requires actual successful secret-fill completion/guard evidence bound to the consumed secret admission, or already committed authenticated positive outcome.
REFUSED requires trusted prewrite no-effect or backend-owned no-send evidence; not a generic TARGET_CHANGED string.
NOT_USED requires authoritative unreached declared step/no-send absence rules; not missing sparse entries.
After invocation with generic/native/cancel/transport uncertainty, absence of positive evidence remains UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; replay omits unknown wire entries.
designRulings.leastNewAuthority: No wire change is necessary to remain truthful under the approved conservative design. First ask PO whether completeness of positive guided no-effect/post-fill facts is required beyond current conservative unknown treatment. If so, Aria explicitly proposes one optional BridgeOutcome.secretUse fact with only existing USED or REFUSED values, present only for an actual consumed secretRef fill and bound through the existing owner/fence/context/admission/step/sourceInput identity; absence means no new knowledge. NOT_USED remains backend-owned unreached evidence. This adds no raw value, new status, external selector, model claim or extra release authority.
conditionalContractRules: Generate closed schemas/types/classpath/pins via existing owner; PO must revalidate exact AC1/AC14/AC19/design §3/§6 deltas before implementation.

USED emitted only after trusted password primitive success; retain it across later outcome delivery/liveness failures if known. REFUSED emitted only from typed structural prewrite fact or pre-invocation no-send; generic after-start errors omit it.
Backend independently validates secret admission and fact/state compatibility; allows a known USED with later uncertain overall action, does not allow a model-supplied fact.
Commit usage idempotently and monotonically; later unknown/refusal cannot overwrite earlier USED. Real callback/ack loss requires its own evidence; ACK_LOST label is insufficient.
Negative/fabricated mismatched fact, actual partial/kill/timeout/native generic and positive completed-fill-with-later-failure tests plus Core/PG/child join required.
designRulings.alternativeForPO: Explicitly retain conservative UNKNOWN_OUTCOME completeness limits without any new field; document that decision rather than deriving missing facts from error labels.
